fatal_errors: The proposed HEO overlayer is not the target intervention, which was a closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning, and Bayesian-optimisation campaign.

The mechanism is centered on suppressing sintering, although the target evidence found that particle size and sintering alone did not explain post-ageing activity; Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction and synthesis-dependent alloy/support states were central.

The cited evidence supports CO oxidation, moisture tolerance, and sinter resistance of HEO systems, but does not establish NO-poison resistance, hydrocarbon conversion, or performance of an HEO overlayer on a near-equiatomic alloy under multicomponent automotive exhaust.
The baseline assigns unsubstantiated properties to the unmodified catalyst and omits the target Pd/Al2O3 benchmark and random-discovery baseline.
explanation: This is a coherent and testable alternative materials strategy rather than a reconstruction of the hidden study. It addresses low-temperature activity, moisture exposure, thermal ageing, and low PGM use, and its paired control experiment could detect improvements in CO light-off and sintering. However, it omits the actual discovery intervention, detailed synthesis window, severe cyclic lean/rich ageing protocol, near-stoichiometric multicomponent feed, Pd benchmark, and species-resolved performance criteria. Its evidence is relevant to HEO-supported Pt and standalone high-entropy spinels, but extrapolation to a porous HEO overlayer on a multi-principal-element alloy and to resistance against NO and hydrocarbon-rich exhaust is not demonstrated. The thermodynamic assertion that configurational disorder simply lowers overall Gibbs free energy is also oversimplified. A stronger test would measure post-ageing NO, CO, C3H6, and i-C5H12 conversion under the specified exhaust mixture and distinguish electronic-site reconstruction from mere particle-size retention.
